title: Closing a project: practices applied and judging the process
blurb: Name the practice a closing action applies, and judge whether a project is being closed effectively: handover, benefits, lessons, follow-on actions and records.
question: A new online service goes live and the project manager requests closure, but nobody has checked that the operational team can handle the cases the service passes to them. Is the project being closed effectively, and why?

teach.body: Practitioner papers ask which practice a closing action applies, using table 19.3; the official extracts examiners quote link closing a project to the business case, plans, quality and organizing practices. They also ask whether closure is effective. Judge that against the objectives in 19.2: user acceptance, the business able to support the products, performance reviewed against baselines, benefits assessed and reviews planned, follow-on actions for open issues and risks, and an orderly close.

teach.h: How closing a project applies the practices
head: Practice
What happens at closure (table 19.3)
rows: Performance assessed; business case updated with actual costs and benefits and a forecast of benefits still to come
Product register checked for the final stage's products, used for lessons and the end project report, then closed
Quality register checked for the final stage's quality activities, then closed; QMA reviewed for closure needs
Team performance and well-being reviewed; communication, change and commercial approaches reviewed for closure needs, such as who to notify
teach.caption: Paraphrased from the official extracts. Note that reviewing the communication approach for closure sits under ORGANIZING here.

root.label: What did the PM check or close?

teach.body: Effective closure checks that users accept the project product and that the business can support it after the project ends. It reviews performance against the baselines, assesses benefits already realized and updates the benefits management approach so post-project reviews happen. It gives every open issue and risk a follow-on action recommendation, secures and archives records, and, in a premature close, closes in an orderly way rather than abandoning the work.

rows.label: Handover
values: Live with no one ready to run it

rows.label: Benefits
values: Project kept open to measure them

rows.label: Open items
values: Closed or left without an owner

teach.caption: The project plans post-project benefits reviews; the business carries them out after the project has closed.

teach.h: What happens to open issues and risks

steps.label:
Included in the
end project report

teach.caption: Open items are not simply closed when the project ends; each gets a recommendation for whoever takes it on.

teach.body: As Permits Online closes, project manager Hannah Okoro updates the business case with actual costs and benefits so far (business case), checks and closes the product and quality registers (plans, quality), and reviews the communication, change and commercial approaches so the contact centre, the trade union and Kestrel Lane are told about closure, a lesson from the waste app launch (organizing). An open risk about winter demand on the telephone route gets a follow-on action recommendation. Benefits reviews are left to the business.

teach.text: Traps: (1) Reviewing the communication, change and commercial approaches at closure is listed under ORGANIZING in table 19.3, not under a 'people practice' (there is none). (2) The product register (plans) and quality register (quality) are both closed: do not swap them. (3) The project plans post-project benefits reviews; it does not stay open to carry them out. (4) A premature close still runs closing a project, tailored, to salvage work and make products safe.

items: Table 19.3: business case (updated with actuals and remaining forecast), plans (product register closed), quality (quality register closed, QMA reviewed), organizing (team reviewed, who to notify).
Judge closure against 19.2: acceptance, supportable products, baselines reviewed, benefits reviews planned, follow-on actions, orderly close.
Records are secured and archived; open issues and risks get follow-on action recommendations.

summary: You can now say which practice any closing a project action applies, using table 19.3. You can also judge whether a closure is effective and pick the reason that explains the verdict.

A.q: Calderbrook Borough Council's Permits Online project is in its final stage. Project manager Hannah Okoro checks the product register to confirm all the final stage's products have been delivered, uses it as input to lessons and the end project report, and then closes it. Which practice is the 'closing a project' process applying?
options: Quality
Plans
Progress
Business case
A.why: Table 19.3: the plans practice is applied in closing a project when the product register is checked for the final stage's products, used for lessons and the end project report, and closed.

whyNot.0: Quality is applied by checking and closing the quality register, not the product register.
whyNot.2: Progress is not the practice table 19.3 links to checking the product register.
whyNot.3: The business case practice is applied by updating the business case with actual costs and benefits.

A.q: As Permits Online closes, Hannah Okoro assesses how the project performed and updates the business case with the actual costs, the benefits achieved so far (processing now takes two days) and a forecast of the benefits still to come. Which practice is the 'closing a project' process applying?
options: The progress practice
The plans practice
The organizing practice
The business case practice
A.why: Table 19.3: the business case practice is applied when performance is assessed and the business case is updated with actual costs and benefits and a forecast of benefits yet to be realized.

whyNot.0: Progress is not the practice table 19.3 links to updating the business case.
whyNot.1: Plans is applied by checking and closing the product register.
whyNot.2: Organizing is applied by reviewing the team and the approaches that say who to notify.

A.q: Before Permits Online closes, Hannah Okoro reviews the communication, change and commercial management approaches to work out who must be told the project is closing, including the contact centre, the trade union and Kestrel Lane Digital. Which practice is the 'closing a project' process applying?
options: Organizing
Progress
Business case
Issues
A.why: Table 19.3 lists reviewing the communication, change and commercial management approaches for closure requirements, such as who to notify, under the organizing practice.

whyNot.1: Progress is not the practice table 19.3 links to reviewing who to notify.
whyNot.2: The business case practice is applied by updating the business case with actuals and forecasts.
whyNot.3: Issues concerns the issue register and issue approach, not who to notify of closure.

B.q: As Permits Online closes, Hannah Okoro checks the quality register to confirm that the final stage's quality activities, including the independent accessibility audit and the IT health check, were performed. She reviews the quality management approach for any closure needs and closes the register. Which practice is the 'closing a project' process applying?
options: Plans
Progress
Quality
Organizing
B.why: Table 19.3: the quality practice is applied when the quality register is checked and closed and the quality management approach is reviewed for closure requirements.

whyNot.0: Plans is applied by checking and closing the product register, not the quality register.
whyNot.1: Progress is not the practice table 19.3 links to the quality register.
whyNot.3: Organizing is applied by reviewing the team and who to notify.

B.q: As Permits Online prepares to close, an open risk remains that the telephone-assisted route may be overwhelmed during the first winter permit renewals. What should Hannah Okoro do about this risk at closure?
options: Keep the project open until the first winter has passed
Record a follow-on action recommendation for it
Close the risk, as the project is about to end
Transfer it to Kestrel Lane's own risk register
B.why: A closing objective is to make sure open issues and risks have follow-on action recommendations, which are included in the end project report (19.2).

whyNot.0: A project should end at a clear point; open risks are passed on with recommendations rather than keeping the project open.
whyNot.2: The risk does not disappear at closure; it needs a follow-on action recommendation.
whyNot.3: The supplier does not own the council's service risk; a recommendation goes to whoever will own the service.

B.q: Ruth Abernethy, head of parking services, asks who will check, after Permits Online has closed, whether permit calls to the contact centre have halved within a year of launch. Which answer is correct?
options: Hannah Okoro, before she requests project closure
Priya Lal, as part of evaluating the project
Kestrel Lane, when its build contract is closed
The business, under the updated benefits approach
B.why: Post-project benefits reviews are planned in the project, with the benefits management approach updated at closure, and carried out by the business afterwards (19.2, 19.3).

whyNot.0: The PM plans post-project reviews but does not carry them out; a year after launch is after closure.
whyNot.1: Evaluate the project looks at project performance at closure; it cannot measure a benefit due a year later.
whyNot.2: The supplier does not own the council's benefits; the business does.

C.q: The paper permit process at Calderbrook is switched off and Hannah Okoro requests project closure. Ruth Abernethy's team has not yet been trained to handle the exception cases the online service passes to them, and this has not been checked. Is the project being closed effectively, and why?
options: Yes, because Kestrel Lane will keep hosting the service under contract
Yes, because the service passed its IT health check before going live
No, because closure should ensure the business can support the products
No, because the paper route should run until all benefits are realized
C.why: An objective of closing a project is to make sure the business can support the products once the project has closed (19.2). Untrained staff for the exception cases fail that test.

whyNot.0: Hosting covers the technology, not the council staff who must handle the exception cases.
whyNot.1: Passing the health check shows the product is fit to go live; it does not show the business can operate it.
whyNot.3: Benefits are realized after closure; the failing is the business's readiness, not the timing of the paper route.

C.q: At the close of Permits Online, Hannah Okoro deletes the project's shared drive and email folders, reasoning that the council should not keep data it no longer needs. Is this an appropriate way to close the project, and why?
options: Yes, because the digital and data approach covers data after closure
Yes, because the project log is closed in prepare planned closure
No, because the records should be handed to Kestrel Lane to host
No, because project information should be secured and archived
C.why: In prepare planned closure, the PM makes sure all project information is secured and archived, so the project can be audited and its lessons and records used later (19.4.1).

whyNot.0: The digital and data management approach does describe data after the project, but it does not justify deleting the project's records.
whyNot.1: The project log is closed, but closing is not deleting; records are secured and archived.
whyNot.2: Archiving is the council's responsibility for its own project records, not the supplier's.

C.q: During the private beta, the government announces a national permit platform that councils must use, and the Permits Online project board decides to close the project early. Hannah Okoro switches off the beta service safely, passes the user research findings to the national platform team, and documents which products were completed and which abandoned. Is this an appropriate application of 'prepare premature closure', and why?
options: Yes, because it salvages useful work and agrees what is abandoned
Yes, because the PM decides when a project should be closed early
No, because an early close skips the closing a project process
No, because products must first be accepted by the operations team
C.why: Prepare premature closure records the request, salvages anything useful, makes products safe and agrees what is complete and what is abandoned, so the close is orderly (19.4.2).

whyNot.1: The verdict is right, but the board, not the PM, triggers a premature close; here the board did.
whyNot.2: Closing a project is still run, tailored, in a premature close.
whyNot.3: Unfinished beta products are made safe or abandoned; they are not handed to operations as if complete.

reteach.title: Four registers and approaches to tidy
reteach.question: Picture the PM's closing checklist. Which item belongs to which practice?

blocks.body: Business case: update it with actual costs and benefits and the forecast of those still to come. Plans: check the product register for the final stage's products, then close it. Quality: check and close the quality register and review the quality approach for closure needs. Organizing: review the team's performance and well-being, and check the communication, change and commercial approaches for who to notify.

blocks.text: Judging closure: can the business support the products, are benefits reviews planned for after closure, do open items have follow-on actions, and are records archived? A 'no' to any of these makes closure ineffective.

explain.h: Business case and plans at closure
explain.body: Business case: performance is assessed and the business case updated with actual costs and benefits and a forecast of remaining benefits. Plans: the product register is checked to confirm the final stage's products were delivered, feeds lessons and the end project report, and is closed.

test.q: Priya Lal, who provides project assurance on Permits Online, asks Hannah Okoro which closing action applies the plans practice. Which action does?
options: Checking and closing the product register
Updating the business case with actual costs
Checking and closing the quality register
Reviewing team performance and well-being
test.why: Table 19.3: in closing a project, the plans practice is applied by checking and closing the product register.

whyNot.1: Updating the business case applies the business case practice.
whyNot.2: Checking and closing the quality register applies the quality practice.
whyNot.3: Reviewing team performance and well-being applies the organizing practice.

explain.body: Quality: the quality register is checked for the final stage's quality activities and closed, and the quality approach is reviewed for closure needs. Organizing: team performance and well-being are reviewed for lessons and the end project report, and the communication, change and commercial approaches are reviewed for who to notify.

test.q: As Permits Online closes, Hannah Okoro reviews how the council staff and Kestrel Lane's team performed and how their well-being held up, as input to lessons and the end project report. Which practice is the 'closing a project' process applying?
options: Progress
Organizing
Quality
Business case
test.why: Table 19.3 links reviewing project team performance, health and well-being at closure to the organizing practice.

whyNot.0: Progress is not the practice table 19.3 links to reviewing the team.
whyNot.2: Quality is applied through the quality register and quality approach.
whyNot.3: The business case practice is applied by updating the business case.

explain.body: Closure is effective when users accept the product, the business can support it, and benefits already realized are assessed with the benefits management approach updated so that post-project reviews take place. Keeping a project open to measure later benefits is not effective.

test.q: Graham Pell, executive for Permits Online, wants closure to handle benefits properly. Which arrangement best meets the closing objective on benefits?
options: Keeping the project open until all benefits are measured
Asking the executive to measure every benefit before closure
Updating the benefits approach for post-project reviews
Dropping benefits reviews once the service is accepted
test.why: A closing objective is to assess benefits already realized and update the benefits management approach so post-project benefits reviews take place after closure (19.2).

whyNot.0: Projects should end at a clear point; later benefits are reviewed by the business after closure.
whyNot.1: Many benefits arise after closure, so they cannot all be measured before it.
whyNot.3: Benefits reviews still need to happen; acceptance of the service does not prove the benefits.

explain.body: Good closure learns from the past: it reviews the project log for lessons, checks the approaches for who to notify, and secures and archives records. Calderbrook's waste app was launched without the contact centre being told, so closure communications matter here.

root.label: Who must know we are closing?

test.q: Calderbrook's waste collection app was launched without the contact centre being told, causing a week of complaints. Which closing action on Permits Online best reflects that lesson?
options: Archiving the project records in the PMO's system
Closing the risk register before the service goes live
Comparing the project's estimates with actual costs
Reviewing the communication approach for who to notify
test.why: Table 19.3: at closure the communication, change and commercial management approaches are reviewed for closure requirements, such as who to notify, which directly addresses the earlier failure.

whyNot.0: Archiving records is good practice, but it does not make sure the contact centre is told.
whyNot.1: Closing registers early does not address notification and leaves open risks without follow-on actions.
whyNot.2: Comparing estimates with actuals improves future estimating, not who is told about the change.
